title: Enhanced approach to calculation of cluster integrals for lattice models of matter
authors: M. V. Ushcats, S. Yu. Ushcats
abstract: The study is devoted to enhancing the existing techniques of calculating Mayer's expansion cluster integrals for lattice models of matter. Two important optimizations are proposed: simplifying the calculation of the integrand at each integration point and reducing the number of such integration points due to eliminating physically identical configurations. Based on those optimizations, new data on high-order cluster integrals are obtained for a number of 2D and 3D lattice models.
summary: This paper presents significant algorithmic improvements for calculating high-order cluster integrals in lattice models using Mayer's expansion. By optimizing both the calculation at each integration point and by drastically reducing the required phase-space volume, the authors obtain new data for 2D and 3D systems. This advances the theoretical understanding of critical phenomena and phase transitions in these classical statistical mechanical models.
main_problem: The study focuses on enhancing computational techniques for calculating Mayer's expansion cluster integrals for lattice models of matter.
main_result: The proposed optimizations significantly reduce the required number of integration points and allow for the calculation of high-order cluster integrals (up to $n=9$) for 2D and 3D lattice models.
method: Two main optimizations are introduced: simplifying integrand calculations at each point by exploiting phase-space independence, and drastically reducing the integration volume by accounting for physically identical configurations.
model_or_system: The research applies to general lattice models of matter (e.g., lattice gases, Ising model) analyzed using Mayer's cluster expansion formalism. The results are presented as exact polynomial forms in terms of the Mayer function $f(T)$.
key_observables: Reducible and irreducible cluster integrals ($b_n$ and $ eta_k$), which serve as power coefficients in the Mayer expansion of the partition function.
important_parameters: The order of the cluster integral ($n$), temperature dependence via $f(T)$, and lattice dimensionality (2D and 3D).
main_assumptions: The method assumes that the Mayer's function can be simplified to take only a few discrete values, allowing the integrals to be expressed as polynomials in $f(T)$.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate relationships between connected diagrams and reducible/irreducible integrals. One figure shows magnetization curves approaching spontaneous magnetization as more irreducible integrals are included.
paper_structure: The paper develops theoretical optimizations for calculating cluster integrals, presents the enhanced computational framework (including combinatorial weight reductions), derives new data tables for high-order integrals in various lattice models, and discusses implications for phase transition analysis.
why_interesting: While focused on classical statistical mechanics, the rigorous development of advanced summation techniques and handling of complex combinatorics is mathematically relevant to developing efficient simulation methods for quantum many-body systems.

figures.caption: Figure 3. (Colour online) Magnetization curves of the 2D square Ising model with nearest-neighbor interactions at 𝑇= 0.8𝑇C (𝑇C is the Curie point). The circle corresponds to the exact spontaneous magnetization point of this Lee–Yang model [3, 5] at the same 𝑇. For each curve, Mayer’s expansion includes 10000 reducible cluster integrals calculated by using the scaling technique [29, 31, 32] on the basis of some limited set of irreducible integrals: a — {𝛽1, 𝛽2}; b — {𝛽1, 𝛽2, 𝛽3, 𝛽4, 𝛽5, 𝛽6}; c — {𝛽1, 𝛽2, 𝛽3, 𝛽4, 𝛽5, 𝛽6, 𝛽7, 𝛽8}.
